why: Nothing in the archive has run on a real 486 or any other physical PC. Every boot and every program ran in QEMU (`-cpu 486`) or headless DOSBox Staging.
The native track names them as test targets in `docs/DIRECTION.md`; neither has booted the image.
Only QEMU's SeaBIOS and a floppy image were tried. IDE and hard-disk boot were not (PR #6).

what: Other DPMI hosts and memory managers.
why: Only CWSDPMI under DOSBox's own DOS. EMM386, QEMM and a Windows 9x DOS box were not tried (PRs #3, #4 and #7).
The fonts follow the era's TrueType rules, but Windows 3.1, 95, NT and OS/2 were not run. Neither were GDI, DirectWrite, macOS, Safari or Firefox (PR #1).

what: The fonts on a DOS screen.
why: The `.DFN` and `.DEM` files were checked against FreeType and a decoder in the tests; no DOS program has drawn them yet.
Audio cannot be checked headless, and nothing here makes any.
CWSDPMI aborts the whole program before any signal handler runs, so it is not recoverable (PR #4). A null write was recovered only under QEMU with FreeDOS (by hand, not in CI).
The generator was tested by serving the files locally. Publishing needs the owner's sign-in, so the live page's controls have not been clicked by the author.
